tools.name: backup
tools.description: Dump the conventioner database into a new folder under ~/conventioner-backups, named for the UTC time it started, and check the dump against the database's own counts taken before and after it. Answers the folder, each collection's document count and the size, never a document. A dump that does not match is removed. Takes no input.

tools.name: list-backups
tools.description: List the dumps under ~/conventioner-backups, newest first: each one's collections, documents, size, whether it was verified, its newest restore drill's verdict and what was derived from it; then any other entry there (a hand-made dump, one a killed backup left unfinished) by name and size; the total, and the dumps past the rule that keeps the newest 5 verified ones, for Daniel to delete by hand. Reads only the folder, no database, and sets it to mode 0700 when it is looser. Takes no input.

tools.name: restore-drill
tools.description: Prove a dump under ~/conventioner-backups restores: restore it into a throwaway local MongoDB (in memory, on the loopback only, behind a password of its own, removed at the end on every path), compare each collection's document count and index names with the dump's manifest, and record the verdict in the dump's folder. Answers PASS or FAIL, each collection that did not match, the time taken and that nothing was left running; never a document. Never reaches the production database. It runs through the machine's heavy-run lock, waiting up to 20 minutes for it, and answers that the machine is busy when it is still held.

backup.description: The backup's name, its UTC start as list-backups gives it (2026-11-08T142305Z); the newest verified backup when left out.

tools.name: rehearse-migrations
tools.description: Rehearse a release's migrations on a dump under ~/conventioner-backups: build the back-end of Chan-Software-Services/Conventioner at the commit named, restore the dump into a throwaway local MongoDB, and run each migration script against it, in order, in a container with no route to production or the internet: with --dry-run first when the script takes one, stopping at a dry run that wrote anything or a run that exited non-zero, and naming the steps not run. Answers each run's exit code and time and, per collection, the counts before and after and the ids of the documents it added, removed or changed, with the top-level fields it changed; never a document, and never a line of a script's output, which goes to logs in the dump's folder for Daniel to read. Removes the MongoDB, the network and the image at the end on every path. Runs only in a checkout of that repository, through the machine's heavy-run lock, waiting up to 20 minutes for it, and answers that the machine is busy when it is still held.

ref.description: The commit of the project's repository whose migrations to rehearse: a commit sha, a branch or a tag, the release's own sha by preference.

migrations.description: The migration scripts to run, in the release's order: each a file's name under back-end/migrations/ at that commit (migrate_phase.py).

backup.description: The backup's name, its UTC start as list-backups gives it (2026-11-08T142305Z); the newest verified backup when left out.

tools.name: prepare-undo
tools.description: Prepare, for Daniel to run, the command that puts one document or one collection of conventioner back as a dump under ~/conventioner-backups holds it, and say what it would change on production now: for one document, whether production's is the same, changed (naming the top-level fields) or gone, or was created since the dump; for a collection, the counts in production and in the dump, the ids the restore would put back, revert and lose, and the index names it would add or drop. Reads production through the read user and writes nothing there; never runs the command, a mongoimport or mongorestore that takes Daniel's own connection string at a read -rs prompt. Writes the document to import and the full lists in the dump's folder, never into the answer.

backup.description: The backup's name, its UTC start as list-backups gives it (2026-11-08T142305Z).

collection.description: The collection to put back, one the backup holds, as backup and list-backups name them (markets).

id.description: One document to put back, by its id as this toolkit's answers print it (a UUID, an ObjectId's hex, an integer or sha256:<12 hex>), or by its _id's hex or UUID; the whole collection when left out.

tools.name: check-integrity
tools.description: Run the invariants saved in Chan-Software-Services/Conventioner's back-end/integrity/invariants.json, read at the ref named (origin/main, what production runs, when left out), against conventioner on production through the read user, read-only: each invariant is an aggregation pipeline whose every output document is one violation. Answers the commit read and, per invariant, PASS, or FAIL with the count (>10,000 at the cap) and at most 50 ids of the documents that break it, or the error it ran into; never a document. Refuses, before it connects, a malformed file and any invariant that could write or run code on the server. Runs only in a checkout of that repository.

ref.description: The commit of the project's repository to read the invariants file from: a branch, a tag or a commit sha; origin/main, what production runs, when left out.

invariants.description: The invariants to run, by name (application-market-exists); every invariant in the file when left out.
